title: TSMC 2nm node climbs to 20% of wafer revenue by Q2 2027
body: TSMC's second-quarter 2026 results put the 2-nanometer node at 3% of wafer revenue in its first meaningful quarter, inside a record print — US$40.20 billion in revenue, up 36% year-over-year, with net income up 77.4% and a 67.7% gross margin. The prediction is that 2nm repeats the trajectory its predecessor traced: 3nm debuted as a small single-digit slice and now holds 30% of wafer revenue, and the company is telegraphing the same steepness for 2nm — CFO Wendell Huang explicitly guided Q3 to US$44.6-45.8 billion on "the steep ramp-up of our 2-nanometer technology," and the 2026 capital-spending plan was raised to US$60-64 billion, spending that only pays back if leading-edge output scales fast. The demand side is already committed: AI accelerator programs at NVIDIA and AMD, flagship smartphone silicon, and on-device NPU roadmaps all queue for the same leading-edge wafers, and TSMC describes demand as rationed by supply rather than by price. Within four reported quarters of its debut — that is, in the quarter ending June 2027 — 2nm should reach roughly a fifth of wafer revenue, displacing 3nm as the growth engine the same way 3nm displaced 5nm.

reasoning.given: Q3 guidance leans on a steep 2nm ramp and 2026 capex was raised to US$60-64B to scale that node
reasoning.so_that: 2nm follows 3nm's ramp curve and crosses 20% of wafer revenue within four reported quarters of debut
reasoning.landing: by Q2 2027; TSMC quarterly report discloses 2nm at 20% or more of wafer revenue
reasoning.plain_language: TSMC's newest chip process just earned its first revenue; if it grows like the previous generation, it becomes a fifth of sales within a year.

summary: TSMC's record Q2 2026 showed 2nm contributing 3% of wafer revenue in its debut quarter, with Q3 guidance built on a steep 2nm ramp and capex raised to US$60-64B. Following the adoption curve 3nm traced to its current 30% share, 2nm is predicted to reach 20% of wafer revenue by Q2 2027.
